title: The nine that went back
material: Nine empty cases, still bolted to the floor of a room that has been closed since June, with their lighting still on a timer that switches at four. The mounts are still in them, cut to the shape of what stood on them, and the felt is unfaded in nine outlines where the objects sat since 1974. The museum's photographs of the nine exist and are not available. The labels have not been changed. The room is Edwardian, refitted once, and smells of the carpet.
occasion: Nine objects held here since 1907 went home in June after a claim that took eleven years and two refusals. The museum has never returned anything before and holds forty thousand more acquired in the same decade by the same means. The room reopens on 14 October with the objects gone and the cases still in it, and nobody has decided what a room in that state is.
when: The room reopens on 14 October. The objects left on 2 June. The claim ran eleven years.
where: The south room of the Harnwell Museum, which is the room they were in.
means: The museum's own workshop, six weeks, the one process they have in the building. No outside supplier: a purchase order over two thousand goes to the board, and the board is where things get softened.
atStake: Forty thousand objects in the same building were acquired the same way and four other institutions are watching. What is unsettled is not whether the nine come back — they are already home — but whether the return is recorded as a claim that was won or as a kindness that was performed, and a room can say either without a word in it.
fear: That it comes out as an apology. An apology would be accepted here and would be insulting there, and it is the one register that makes everybody comfortable, which is how it gets chosen.
pressures: The eleven years want to be stated, and stating them turns the room into an argument with the board, which converts a return into a grievance and hands the four watching institutions a reason to call it a campaign.

An empty case is a ready-made gesture. The sector has used it often enough in five years to have a shorthand for it, and the shorthand is available here for nothing, already legible, and says almost the opposite of what happened.
Absence reads as a gap unless something is done to it, and the fastest thing to do to a gap is fill it, which undoes the only true thing in the room.
The institution's own conduct wants to be visible somewhere — somebody did fight for eleven years — and there is no way to make that visible that does not also make the museum the subject.
refusals: No image of the nine. The museum still holds the photographs and still owns the rights, and using them would be the museum exercising, on this of all things, the last piece of ownership it has left.
Nothing that could be read as an instruction to other claimants. This is one room and one claim, and a room that generalises has started speaking for people who have not asked it to.
Nothing that reads as a gift given. That is what the museum's own account has always implied and what eleven years were spent refusing.
Not the outlines in the felt. They are the most affecting thing in the room and they are a picture of possession, made by the objects sitting where they were put.
notes: The lighting timer still switches at four and nobody has turned it off. The education team have to rewrite the worksheet by 7 October and have not been told what to write.
